items.title: Sergio Perez praises Colton Herta impact - but has no say over 2027 Cadillac F1 team-mate choice
items.summary: Sergio Perez has insisted he will have no say on his Cadillac Formula 1 team-mate for 2027 after signing a new contract ahead of the Mexican Grand Prix.

items.title: Why “ignorance is a superpower” for Kimi Antonelli, according to Daniel Ricciardo
items.summary: Daniel Ricciardo believes Kimi Antonelli’s age and innocence is what has made him so successful in the 2026 Formula 1 season. Nine victories so far in his sophomore F1 campaign have taken Antonelli to the brink of his maiden world title. All the Mercedes driver needs to be crowned in Sunday’s Mexican Grand Prix is ninth place, or for neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton to win.

items.title: Isack Hadjar admits after criticising Red Bull: "There's stuff that I should have kept for myself"
items.summary: After the United States Grand Prix, Isack Hadjar was critical of Red Bull's execution, as was Max Verstappen. Both drivers were unhappy with the strategy and, on top of that, were hampered by two problems that have been troubling the Formula 1 team for a long time: technical issues with the team radio and problematic starts. "I have poor radio, I don't even know what's happening.

items.title: Why F1's new regulations make the Mexican GP an even bigger challenge
items.summary: At 2,286 metres above sea level, the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez is by far the highest-altitude venue on the Formula 1 calendar. This naturally means thinner air, which presents a unique challenge at the Mexican Grand Prix for teams and manufacturers in two ways.

items.title: George Russell predicts key Ferrari "advantage" at F1 Mexican GP
items.summary: Mercedes driver George Russell reckons Ferrari has "quite an advantage" at F1's Mexican Grand Prix with its turbo design, while Charles Leclerc still believes Mercedes has the best car "wherever we go". Mexico's capital megalopolis sits on a 2250m plateau, which gives the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez one of the most unique engineering challenges.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: “I’m built differently” as he eyes F1 career into 2030s
items.summary: Seven-time Formula 1 world champion Lewis Hamilton insists he is “built differently” as he discusses the idea of extending his career long enough to race at the new African Grand Prix. F1 recently announced a 10-year deal with Rwanda to host a race at a new circuit near Kigali, with the event expected to join the calendar in the early 2030s.

items.title: Max Verstappen discusses toll of F1 calendar after two drivers fall ill
items.summary: Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says it is "normal" for F1 drivers and team members to fall ill at this stage of the season after two drivers missed Thursday's media day in Mexico City.

items.title: Max Verstappen jokes about Daniel Ricciardo's Le Mans ambition: "He's a smart man picking me!"
items.summary: Max Verstappen has joked that former Red Bull team-mate Daniel Ricciardo is a "smart man" for picking him in a potential trio for a future Le Mans 24 Hour challenge. Ricciardo has not taken part in any racing series since leaving F1 for the second time having raced for Red Bull's sister RB squad in 2024.

items.title: Max Verstappen responds to Daniel Ricciardo’s Le Mans dream team call
items.summary: Max Verstappen has joked that his former team-mate Daniel Ricciardo is "a smart man" for picking him for his dream Le Mans line-up. In fact, he revealed that the pair of them had already discussed the possibility of it. In a recent interview with the Beyond the Grid podcast, the Australian talked about his time at Red Bull and his exit from Formula 1.

items.title: Alex Albon dismisses Fernando Alonso criticism: 'F1 has no more pay drivers'
items.summary: Alex Albon says Fernando Alonso's criticism on his clash in Austin was "not nice to hear" but dismisses the Spaniard's claims that the bottom third of the grid is lacking quality.

items.title: Charles Leclerc defends Alex Albon after Fernando Alonso's scathing criticism
items.summary: Ferrari Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc has rejected Fernando Alonso's claim that the standard of driving at the back of the grid is low, insisting the level is "very, very high" across the field.

items.title: Charles Leclerc reveals what he really wants from final five F1 races of 2026
items.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc says he is “not obsessed” with finishing second in the Formula 1 drivers’ championship, despite being just nine points off the position with five races to go. While Kimi Antonelli is expected to wrap up his championship campaign this weekend at the Mexican Grand Prix, the fight for second place is alive and well between a number of drivers.

items.title: George Russell makes defiant Mercedes statement as Kimi Antonelli nears world title
items.summary: Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has insisted that, despite an inconsistent 2026 season, he still has “a good 12 to 15 years” left in the championship. The Briton arrives in Mexico City second in the drivers' standings, albeit 123 points off his young team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who can take his first championship title this weekend.

items.title: George Russell on F1 title loss: 'This year won't break me'
items.summary: George Russell has insisted his career will 'not be defined' and he 'won't be broken' by failing to secure a maiden Formula 1 world title this season.

items.title: Fernando Alonso doubles down on poor F1 driving standards: "We all know who we're talking about"
items.summary: After Fernando Alonso was hit by Alexander Albon on the opening lap of the US Grand Prix in Austin – which, according to Aston Martin's chief trackside officer Mike Krack, cost him a considerable amount of downforce – the two-time world champion was highly critical of the current driving standards in Formula 1. "When you start at the back, there is always this risk.

items.title: Who would replace Charles Leclerc at Ferrari if he misses a race for his baby’s birth?
items.summary: Charles Leclerc insists he will not miss a grand prix when his first child is born, but Ferrari has reportedly lined up a stand-in in case plans change. The Monegasque and his wife Alexandra are expecting their first baby during the last weeks of the 2026 Formula 1 season.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli backed to surpass Sebastian Vettel's four F1 titles by Guenther Steiner
items.summary: Former Haas Formula 1 team principal Guenther Steiner believes Kimi Antonelli will go on to have a more successful F1 career than four-time champion Sebastian Vettel. Antonelli is on the verge of winning his maiden F1 championship, and will be crowned at this weekend's Mexican Grand Prix if he finishes in the top nine.

items.title: Every LEGO F1 set you can buy right now: £10.99 to £199.99
items.summary: LEGO currently boasts a total of 31 Formula 1 sets on its UK and US stores, from a £10.99 McLaren for young children to £199.99 Technic models of championship-winning cars. Here is every set an F1 fan like yourself you buy right now.

items.title: F1 Mexico GP: Friday schedule, weather forecast and how to watch
items.summary: Formula 1 heads to Mexico City this weekend with Kimi Antonelli on the verge of securing his first world championship after dominating the United States Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver claimed his ninth victory of the season in Austin and now leads team-mate George Russell by 123 points, with Lewis Hamilton a further point behind.

items.title: Unwell Kimi Antonelli skips F1 Mexico GP media day
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli won’t attend Formula 1’s Mexico Grand Prix on Thursday due to feeling unwell, the Mercedes team has revealed. A spokesperson for the Anglo-German outfit told media that the championship leader was “feeling under the weather” due to a “viral illness” he has been recovering, with the FIA therefore excusing him from today’s media activities.

items.title: Why Daniel Ricciardo would consider a comeback at Le Mans
items.summary: Last month marked two years since Daniel Ricciardo’s last motor race to this day, as the eight-time grand prix winner regretfully, discreetly bowed out of Formula 1 – but is his career over?

items.title: The 10 key moments that defined Sergio Perez's F1 career
items.summary: This weekend, Sergio Perez joins the exclusive club of drivers with at least 300 Formula 1 race starts, a milestone achieved by legends such as Michael Schumacher, Jenson Button, and Rubens Barrichello. Throughout this journey, the Mexican driver has experienced several key moments that shaped his history in motorsport... 1.

items.title: Does Daniel Ricciardo regret leaving Red Bull for Renault?
items.summary: Back in July 2018, Daniel Ricciardo was one of the most highly-rated drivers in the Formula 1 paddock. He had been in the Red Bull family for a decade, since his early junior single-seater career, and was now spearheading the brand’s effort in the world championship.

items.title: Cadillac 'honoured' to have Sergio Perez as special 300th race celebration planned for Mexico GP
items.summary: General Motors president Mark Reuss has praised Cadillac Formula 1 driver Sergio Perez ahead of his 300th race in the series, insisting it is "an honour" to have the Mexican on side.

items.title: Sebastian Vettel reveals why BMW didn't want him – but Red Bull did
items.summary: Sebastian Vettel has opened up about his early years in Formula 1 in the new ARD documentary Being Sebastian Vettel – and how German manufacturer BMW initially supported him before ultimately letting him go. The four-time F1 world champion said: "In the end, the whole BMW story didn't really work out as originally planned.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli reveals plans to launch his own racing academy outside F1
items.summary: At just 20 years old, Andrea Kimi Antonelli is currently busy making records on his second season of his Formula 1 career. But apparently, casually dominating the 2026 World Championship in a Mercedes isn't quite enough to keep the Italian phenom occupied.

items.title: Christian Horner admits he doesn't need F1 return after £67 million Red Bull payout
items.summary: When a high-profile Formula 1 executive is shown the door, the rumour mill immediately shifts to where they will land next. But in the case of Christian Horner, his departure from Red Bull Racing in 2025 came with a golden parachute so immense that it completely rewrote his career trajectory.

items.title: Mark Webber's Red Bull exit branded "disrespectful" as Daniel Ricciardo praised
items.summary: Red Bull Racing has a long, highly complicated history with Australian drivers. Mark Webber helped build the team's winning foundation during Sebastian Vettel's championship years, while Daniel Ricciardo took the baton and led the garage at the dawn of the turbo-hybrid era.

items.title: Christian Horner reveals why Netflix made him the villain of "Drive to Survive"
items.summary: Before Netflix brought its cameras into the Formula 1 paddock, team principals were largely viewed as calculating, stoic directors operating quietly from the pitwall. By the time Christian Horner left, the role had evolved into something entirely different.

items.title: Daniel Ricciardo opens door to racing return with Max Verstappen at Le Mans
items.summary: Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo has revealed he would consider a one-off appearance at the Le Mans 24 Hours and named his former Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen as his first choice to share a car with.
